name: Orazio Grassi
summary: Jesuit mathematician and astronomer who taught at the Collegio Romano and engaged in scientific controversy with Galileo Galilei.

name: Christopher Clavius
summary: Jesuit mathematician and astronomer who institutionalized physico-mathematics in Jesuit education and mentored Grassi.

name: Galileo Galilei
summary: Italian astronomer and physicist who debated Grassi on the nature of comets and published the Assayer.

name: Tycho Brahe
summary: Danish astronomer whose geo-heliocentric cosmology and observations influenced Jesuit science.

name: Collegio Romano
summary: Flagship Jesuit university in Rome where Grassi studied and taught mathematics.

name: Society of Jesus
summary: Catholic religious order to which Grassi and Clavius belonged.

name: Mathematica (1623 manuscript)
summary: Student notes from Grassi's 1623 lectures on spherical astronomy held at the University of Oklahoma.

name: Libra astronomica ac philosophica
summary: 1619 book by Grassi published under the pseudonym Lotario Sarsi debating Galileo on comets.

name: Ratio ponderum librae et simbellae
summary: 1626 book by Grassi responding to Galileo's Assayer.

name: Disputatio astronomica de tribus cometis anni MDCXVIII
summary: 1619 anonymous lecture publication by Grassi on the comets of 1618.

name: De iride disputatio optica
summary: 1617 publication by Grassi on optics published under his student's name.

name: The Assayer
summary: 1623 book by Galileo Galilei rebutting Grassi's arguments on comets.

name: Savona
summary: Italian city where Orazio Grassi was born.

name: Rome
summary: City where the Collegio Romano was located and where Grassi taught.
